description: describeStatus rules for the normative status text tables (docs/MCPWARP.md section 7). One table file per locale (en.json, de.json, es.json, fr.json, ja.json, zh-CN.json), every one with exactly the key set of en.json; cases.json holds input -> expected examples every SDK runs, except hostOnlyCases (below); the hostOnly keys are optional in an SDK's tables.

keyFormat.rule: <state>.<code>, with the literal 'none' when the status carries no code. The <state>.<code> keys of en.json are exactly the legal (state, code) pairings of a TunnelStatus; since v0.7.0 the seven multi-service keys (multiService below) follow them, host-only since v0.8.0 (hostOnly below).
keyFormat.value: {label, detail?} = describeStatus({state, code}) with no lastError. detail is left out when it would equal label.
keyFormat.stateLabel: states[state] = label of any <state>.<code> key starting with '<state>.'; every key of one state has the same label
keyFormat.codeSentence: codes[code] = detail ?? label of any <state>.<code> key ending in '.<code>'; every key of one code has the same sentence (INTERNAL pairs with connecting and error, and connecting.INTERNAL and error.INTERNAL carry the same sentence in every locale)

multiService.scope: Since v0.8.0 informative host guidance (D-2026-10-24-01): no SDK ships a multi-service controller. The keys in hostOnly are OPTIONAL in an SDK's tables and an SDK runner compares only the other keys; the locale files keep them, with their values, for hosts (CLI, desktop) that multiplex several services on one connection.
multiService.serviceLabels: service.<state> = {label} for each ServiceState: pending, active, disabled, rejected, taken_over, unregistered
multiService.noServiceRegistered: lastError.NO_SERVICE_REGISTERED = {label: the locale's error label, detail} = describeStatus({state: "error", code: "INTERNAL", lastError: "No service could be registered."})
multiService.describeStatusRule: state error, code INTERNAL and lastError exactly "No service could be registered.": detail = the lastError.NO_SERVICE_REGISTERED detail instead of the INTERNAL sentence; services is ignored
describeServiceStatus: label = the service.<state> label; an unknown state -> String(state)
rejected: detail = the error.<CODE> detail for INVALID_NAME, USERNAME_REQUIRED, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, CONFLICT; the error.UNAUTHORIZED detail for UNAUTHENTICATED, FORBIDDEN; else the error.INTERNAL detail
disabled with code DISABLED: detail = the disabled.DISABLED label
otherwise no detail; lastError is never shown; detail is left out when equal to label

steps: a locale that is not a string resolves to en
tag = locale with surrounding whitespace trimmed, every '_' replaced by '-', lowercased
exact: the first entry of order whose lowercased form equals tag
language: else the first entry of order whose lowercased primary subtag (text before the first '-') equals tag's primary subtag

composition: label = states[state] when state is a known state, else the state value as a string
sentence = codes[code] when code is a known code, else none
no sentence (code absent or unknown): detail = lastError, unchanged (no colon rewrite)
code INVALID_CONFIG with a non-empty lastError: detail = invalidConfig composition
any other known code: detail = sentence; lastError is not shown (this includes INVALID_NAME, whose sentence carries the name rule itself)
detail is left out when it is absent, empty, or equal to label

steps: lastError starts with sentence: detail = lastError
else: detail = sentence + colonJoiner[locale] + lastError with lastErrorColonRewrite applied

codeLessError: A status with no code (or a code outside the table) shows lastError as its detail, for any state, unchanged.

hostOffPattern.rule: Before a host can configure the tunnel (no token yet, say) it shows its own status {state: "off", lastError: <host constant>} with no code; describeStatus returns {label: <off label>, detail: <host constant>}.

status.lastError: Add an mcpwarp token in the settings to go online.

expect.label: Off
expect.detail: Add an mcpwarp token in the settings to go online.

lint: the only translated strings equal to the English ones: de states.online ('Online') and es states.error ('Error')
hostOnlyCases: a cases.json case with input.service (describeServiceStatus), or whose input.status carries services (the two lastError.NO_SERVICE_REGISTERED group cases), is host-only: an SDK runner skips it unless the implementation declares host support
